applies_why: The judge text evaluates the Acts 2:30 link by the absence of an explicit naming of whose body is the channel, rather than by weighing the competing chains' footing.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase is 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse.' Reading 1: the judge must compare the whole chains' footing before calling the point open. Reading 2: the judge may call it open because the verse itself does not name the channel.
why: Because it leaves the point open from the text's failure to explicitly name the channel, it applies the retired stating-verse test instead of chain-by-chain footing.
